question: A teacher’s laptop only works when plugged in. Battery health reports normal capacity, but the laptop shuts off instantly when the AC adapter is removed. Which next check best separates a battery fault from a power-delivery or board-level fault?

options.text: Replace the laptop battery immediately because capacity is the only battery-health indicator that matters.
Test with a known-good compatible AC adapter and inspect the DC-in/USB-C charging path before replacing parts.
Reinstall Windows because sudden shutdowns are normally caused by corrupt power plans.
Disable sleep and hibernation so the laptop cannot power off unexpectedly.

explanation: A known-good adapter and charging-path check helps isolate whether the issue is battery, charger, port, or board-level power delivery before parts are replaced.

question: A BYOD tablet can access email but cannot receive required Wi-Fi profiles or app restrictions. The user insists they signed in correctly. Which finding most strongly points to the actual issue?

options.text: The device is enrolled as personal/BYOD but the policy is scoped only to corporate-owned devices.
The device battery is below 50%, so MDM profiles cannot apply.
The user is connected to 5 GHz Wi-Fi rather than 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
The user’s email mailbox is full.

explanation: MDM targeting/scope and ownership type commonly determine whether configuration profiles apply. Email access alone does not prove the device is correctly enrolled for policy.

question: A staff phone connects to Bluetooth headphones but cannot use a wireless hotspot from a laptop beside it. Other phones can use the hotspot. What is the best first support explanation?

options.text: Bluetooth success proves all wireless radios are healthy.
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi/hotspot use different radios/protocols, so each must be tested separately.
The laptop hotspot must be using cellular 5G rather than Wi-Fi.
The phone cannot support both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi at the same time.

explanation: Bluetooth working does not validate Wi-Fi or hotspot capability. Treat each wireless function as a separate symptom path.

question: A workstation shows 169.254.18.22 and cannot access the network. What does this most likely indicate?

The device has self-assigned an APIPA address after failing to get DHCP.
The DNS server has assigned a temporary quarantine address.
The gateway has blocked HTTPS traffic.

explanation: 169.254.x.x is APIPA, usually indicating the client did not receive a DHCP lease.

question: A remote user says the VPN connects, but they cannot reach one internal subnet while other internal apps work. What is the most useful first technical evidence to collect?

RAID 1
RAID 5
